LESSON: AREA

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: GRADE
Strand: MEASUREMENTS
Topic 3.2: Area
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Area, part of MEASUREMENTS in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: How do we use area in real-life situations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Area together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: Uses creativity in work context; as learners use cut-outs of sectors of circles from

locally available materials and find the area.

● Learning to learn: Knows what doing well looks like; as learners use models to find the surface area of cubes, cuboids and

cylinders and derive the formulas for each.

Values:
● Responsibility: Through excellence as learners use models to find the surface area of triangular prisms.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

27

● Socio-Economic and Environmental Issues: Safety; As learners handle different instruments to make cut-outs of sectors from

locally available materials and find the area where they relate the angle of the sector to the area of the circle.

● Socio-Economic and Environmental Issues: Environment & technology; As learners use locally available materials to draw

irregular shapes, for example their palm of hands, feet, leaves etc. and trace on square grid to estimate the area.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner is able to relate the concept of tracing to drawing irregular shapes, for example their palm of hands, feet, leaves in

Creative Arts.
